doc.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025

title: The trumpet as a prop and coming out of his shell
summary: Palmer reflects on teaching in public schools and a 1998 reading to his brother's class.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Over the years I’ve had, especially in middle school-aged, promising musicians but they were really shy. And I saw you speak in an interview and you described yourself as a quiet person. And I used to say to these shy young musicians, “Think of your instrument like a prop, like when an actor gets a cane and a hat they’re transforming themselves.” And I wonder if you ever thought about your trumpet as a prop that allows me to step outside of my regular personality?

Yeah I think the trumpet has that ability more so than other instruments. You know I taught in the public schools for about 12, 13 years and I taught woodwind and brass. I taught clarinet, you know, tenor, alto, trombone, I had some trumpet students. And yeah it’s like the trumpet has a certain magnetism that attracts certain types of people, you know really loud outspoken people or maybe really reserved people that want to have something that’s on the opposite end of what they are. And then you have some that have something that they want to be exactly what that is, you know I want to be loud and

brass, Maynard Ferguson style. And then you have other people, it’s like I really want to make this brass instrument that wants to be loud and high be something that’s more subtle like Chet Baker or, you know somebody else. So yeah for me it’s probably a mix of that. But I say I’ve really gotten a little bit out of my — I mean I’ve gotten older and, you know, developed more as a person and so I’ve kind of come out of my shell that way but I think just being on the educational side of things really opened me up and I’ve really gotten an education. Back in 1998 I went home during one of the holiday breaks, back home to North Carolina. And I have a younger brother who, he was in grade school at the time. And I went to his school and I read a children’s book, a few childrens’ books to his class. He was in about third or fourth grade, I can’t remember what grade he was in. But I went to the library and I read to all of them and just to see their faces really light up after I was reading something to them and saying oh wow, I can make a difference in these young childrens’ lives. Let me learn more about music and maybe I could teach. You know? So just by having that experience it kind of influenced me to — it inspired me to get to a point where I could learn more so I’d be able to share more and that helped me come out of my shell. So I think just being in a classroom so much has kind of helped me not be as shy and be as quiet as I described in what you read.
